ThingDef.label: fragmentation grenades
ThingDef.description: A pre-war military fragmentation grenade. The steel casing shatters into deadly shrapnel upon detonation, sending metal fragments in all directions. Standard issue before the war and still highly valued.

ThingDef.label: plasma grenades
ThingDef.description: An advanced pre-war grenade that releases superheated plasma in a contained sphere. The intense heat vaporizes organic tissue and melts armor. Expensive and rare, but devastatingly effective.

ThingDef.label: pulse grenades
ThingDef.description: A specialized military EMP grenade designed to disable electronic systems and robotics. More powerful than standard EMP grenades, pulse grenades were issued to units expected to face heavy mechanized opposition.

ThingDef.label: cryo grenades
ThingDef.description: An experimental pre-war grenade that releases ultra-cold cryogenic compounds. The sudden temperature drop flash-freezes everything in the blast radius, causing severe frostbite and making materials brittle.

ThingDef.label: nuka grenades
ThingDef.description: An improvised explosive made from Nuka-Cola Quantum bottles. The isotope's natural radioactivity makes it far more destructive than conventional explosives. The distinctive glow gives away its presence, but anyone close enough to see it is already in danger.

ThingDef.label: nuka quantum grenades
ThingDef.description: An enhanced version of the nuka grenade using the rarer Nuka-Cola Quantum variant. The higher isotope concentration creates an even more powerful explosion with additional radiation effects. The blue glow is hypnotic—and lethal.

ThingDef.label: dynamite
ThingDef.description: Pre-war industrial explosive sticks. Originally used for mining and construction, dynamite is still effective for demolition and combat. Burns fast with a short fuse, leaving little time to escape.

ThingDef.label: long fuse dynamite
ThingDef.description: Dynamite sticks with an extended fuse, allowing more time to take cover or set traps. Popular with wasteland trappers and guerrilla fighters who need time to get clear of the blast.

ThingDef.label: bio gas grenades
ThingDef.description: A chemical weapon from before the war, designed to release toxic biological agents. The gas attacks the respiratory system and exposed skin, causing severe damage to organic targets while leaving structures intact.

ThingDef.label: HalluciGen gas grenades
ThingDef.description: A canister of weaponized hallucinogenic gas from HalluciGen, Inc. When deployed, it releases a concentrated cloud of psychoactive compounds that cause severe hallucinations and violent paranoia. Victims often turn on each other in their confusion. A pre-war crowd control weapon with terrifying effectiveness.

ThingDef.label: smoke grenades
ThingDef.description: A tactical smoke grenade used to obscure vision and provide cover. Produces a dense cloud of white smoke that blocks line of sight. Essential for military operations and tactical withdrawals.

ThingDef.label: flashbang grenades
ThingDef.description: A non-lethal stun grenade that produces an intense flash of light and deafening sound. Temporarily blinds and disorients anyone nearby. Popular with law enforcement and special operations teams before the war.

ThingDef.label: acid grenades
ThingDef.description: A chemical grenade that disperses highly corrosive acid upon detonation. The acid eats through armor, flesh, and structural materials indiscriminately. Handle with extreme caution.

ThingDef.label: tincan grenades
ThingDef.description: A crude explosive fashioned from a tin can, gunpowder, and scrap metal. When detonated, the can shatters into jagged shrapnel. Cheap and effective, though unreliable. A staple among wasteland raiders and desperate settlers.

ThingDef.label: piggybank grenades
ThingDef.description: An improvised grenade made from a ceramic piggybank filled with explosives and pre-war coins. The coins become deadly projectiles when the device detonates. Wasteland ingenuity at its finest—making currency literally pay for its weight in blood.

ThingDef.label: pipebombs
ThingDef.description: A simple explosive device constructed from a sealed pipe filled with gunpowder or other propellants. The metal casing becomes deadly shrapnel. Easy to manufacture and devastatingly effective. A favorite among wasteland insurgents.

ThingDef.label: baseball grenades
ThingDef.description: A pre-war baseball gutted and packed with explosives and nails. Throws like the real thing, but explodes on impact. Popular with wasteland gangs for its ease of use and the ironic nostalgia of weaponizing America's pastime.

ThingDef.label: MFC grenades
ThingDef.description: A repurposed microfusion cell rigged to overload and detonate. When the containment fails, it releases a burst of plasma energy. Dangerous to construct, but effective. Wastelanders with technical know-how can turn depleted energy cells into deadly weapons.

ThingDef.label: molotov cocktails
ThingDef.description: A glass bottle filled with flammable liquid and a burning cloth wick. Simple, cheap, and terrifyingly effective at spreading fire. The weapon of choice for rioters, revolutionaries, and desperate wastelanders throughout history.

ThingDef.label: mininukes
ThingDef.description: A small tactical nuclear explosive, small enough to be thrown by hand but powerful enough to level buildings. Highly radioactive and extraordinarily dangerous. Few wastelanders have the resources or insanity to manufacture these.

ThingDef.label: boombug grenades
ThingDef.description: A container of captured boombugs—mutated insects with volatile explosive sacs. When released, they swarm toward heat sources and detonate on contact. Difficult to control but devastating when used correctly. Handle with extreme caution.

ThingDef.label: Holy Hand Grenade of Antioch
ThingDef.description: And Saint Attila raised the hand grenade up on high, saying, "O Lord, bless this thy hand grenade, that with it thou mayst blow thine enemies to tiny bits, in thy mercy." This sacred relic of the old world possesses devastating power—but can only be used once. Count to three. No more, no less.
